skull.name: Skull
skull.desc: The skull protects the brain, holds the eyes and teeth, and shapes the face. Most of its bones are joined tightly; only the lower jaw moves.
good: A helmet on bikes, motorbikes and building sites
bad: Falls and blows to the head

teeth.name: Teeth
teeth.desc: Teeth cut, tear and grind food so it can be swallowed and digested. Their outer enamel is the hardest substance in the body.
good: Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste
bad: Sugary snacks and drinks between meals

spine.name: Spine
spine.desc: A stack of vertebrae that protects the spinal cord, holds up the head and body, and lets you bend and twist. Soft discs between them absorb shocks.
good: Good posture when sitting and using your phone
Exercises that strengthen the core and back
Lifting with your legs, back straight
bad: Lifting heavy loads with a bent back

ribcage.name: Ribcage
ribcage.desc: Twelve pairs of ribs curve from the spine to the breastbone. They protect the heart and lungs and lift with every breath.
bad: Falls and hard blows to the chest

shoulder.name: Shoulder bones
shoulder.desc: The collarbone and shoulder blade connect the arm to the body. Together with the upper arm bone they form the most mobile joint in the body.
good: Strength training for the back and shoulders
bad: Falling onto the shoulder or an outstretched hand
Lifting heavy weights overhead without training
facts: The most mobile in the body

humerus.name: Upper arm bone
humerus.desc: The humerus runs from the shoulder to the elbow. Muscles attached to it lift, push and pull the arm.
bad: Lifting more than you can control

forearm.name: Forearm bones
forearm.desc: The radius and ulna run from the elbow to the wrist. They twist around each other so you can turn your palm up and down.
bad: Repeating the same wrist movement for hours

hand.name: Hand bones
hand.desc: Many small bones make the hand strong and very precise. The thumb can touch every finger, which lets you grip and hold tools.
good: Stretching and moving the fingers during long screen time
bad: Typing or texting for hours without breaks

pelvis.name: Pelvis
pelvis.desc: A bowl of bone that carries the weight of the upper body to the legs and protects the bladder and lower gut. It holds the sockets of the hip joints.
bad: Sitting for many hours without moving

femur.name: Thigh bone
femur.desc: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the body. It carries your weight from the hip to the knee.
bad: Sitting still for most of the day
facts: about a quarter of your height

knee.name: Knee
knee.desc: The largest joint in the body. Ligaments hold it together, the kneecap protects the front and two cartilage cushions called menisci absorb shocks.
bad: Twisting the knee while the foot is planted
Kneeling on hard floors for long
facts: Hinge that also rotates a little

lower_leg.name: Lower leg bones
lower_leg.desc: The tibia (shin bone) carries most of the body's weight, and the thin fibula beside it anchors muscles and steadies the ankle.

foot.name: Foot bones
foot.desc: The foot is built like a flexible arch. It spreads your weight, absorbs shocks and pushes you forward with every step.
good: Shoes that fit and support the arch
Walking barefoot on safe ground sometimes
bad: Uncontrolled diabetes, which harms the feet

bones.name: Bone
bones.desc: Bone is living tissue that supports the body, protects organs and stores calcium. Blood cells are made in the marrow inside some bones.

muscles.name: Muscle
muscles.desc: Skeletal muscles pull on bones to move the body. They also hold your posture and make heat that keeps you warm.
good: Strength exercise at least twice a week
bad: Sitting still for most of the day
Not drinking enough water during exercise

biceps.name: Biceps
biceps.desc: The muscle at the front of the upper arm. It bends the elbow and turns the palm up.

triceps.name: Triceps
triceps.desc: The muscle at the back of the upper arm. It straightens the elbow when you push.

deltoid.name: Deltoid
deltoid.desc: The rounded muscle that caps the shoulder. It lifts the arm forward, sideways and back.
bad: Heavy lifting overhead with poor form
Sleeping on the same shoulder for years

chest_muscles.name: Chest muscles
chest_muscles.desc: The pectoral muscles move the arm across the body and help you push, hug and throw.
bad: Heavy bench pressing without a spotter

abs.name: Abdominal muscles
abs.desc: These muscles hold in the organs, support the spine and help you bend, twist, cough and breathe out hard.

back_muscles.name: Back muscles
back_muscles.desc: Layers of muscles along the spine and shoulder blades. They keep you upright and move the arms, shoulders and trunk.
bad: Long hours hunched over a phone or desk

glutes.name: Buttock muscles
glutes.desc: The gluteal muscles move the hip and keep the pelvis level when you walk, run and climb stairs.

quadriceps.name: Thigh muscles (front)
quadriceps.desc: Four muscles at the front of the thigh. They straighten the knee and are key for walking, jumping and climbing.

hamstrings.name: Hamstrings
hamstrings.desc: Three muscles at the back of the thigh. They bend the knee and help push the leg backwards when you run.

calf.name: Calf muscles
calf.desc: The calf muscles lift the heel, push you forward when you walk and help pump blood back up from the legs.
bad: Sitting or standing still for hours

connective.name: Tendons and ligaments
connective.desc: Tough, rope-like tissues. Tendons join muscle to bone, and ligaments join bone to bone to keep joints stable.

spinal_cord.name: Spinal cord
spinal_cord.desc: A thick bundle of nerves inside the spine that carries messages between the brain and the body. It also handles fast reflexes.
good: Diving only into deep, safe water
bad: Car and motorbike accidents without protection

nerves.name: Nerves
nerves.desc: Nerves are cables of nerve fibres that carry signals between the brain, the spinal cord and every part of the body.
bad: Pressure on a nerve for a long time, like leaning on the elbow

aorta.name: Aorta
aorta.desc: The largest artery. It leaves the heart, arches over it and runs down through the chest and belly, sending oxygen-rich blood to the whole body.

arteries.name: Arteries
arteries.desc: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Their strong, elastic walls stretch with each heartbeat, which you can feel as your pulse.
bad: Too much salt and fatty food

veins.name: Veins
veins.desc: Veins carry blood back to the heart. Small valves inside stop blood from flowing backwards, and leg muscles help push it up.
bad: Sitting or standing still for hours

lymph.name: Lymph vessels and nodes
lymph.desc: A network that drains extra fluid from the tissues back into the blood. Lymph nodes along the way trap germs and help the immune system respond.

skin.name: Skin
skin.desc: The largest organ. It keeps germs and water out, helps control body temperature, makes vitamin D in sunlight and lets you feel touch, heat and pain.
good: Sunscreen and shade in strong sun
bad: Very hot water and harsh soaps
